title: Designated vs Convenience Initialisers

docs.title: Initialization — Initializer Delegation for Class Types

hints: Convenience initialisers must call another initialiser of the same class with `self.init(...)`.
`init(white:)` passes one value three times; `init?(hex:)` checks the format, parses base 16, then extracts channels with shifts and masks.
jsBridge: Designated initialisers set every property. `convenience` initialisers must delegate to one with `self.init(...)`, like overloaded constructors calling a primary one. `init?` can fail and return `nil`, which JS constructors can't.

compass.q: A JS constructor can't return `null`. How would you model "invalid hex" in JS: static factory or throw? What does `init?` give you?
Failable `init?` vs throwing `init() throws`: when should callers learn *why* it failed?
Can a convenience init call another convenience init? Can it call `super.init`?
`UIColor(hex:)` is a common extension. Why is it usually a convenience init?
